questions.q: What does a Salesforce edition actually determine, per this lesson?
options: Which features, customization limits, and automation tools the org has access to — not just a price tag
Only the color scheme of the user interface
Nothing meaningful — all editions are functionally identical
Only how many free trial days the org gets
questions.explain: Edition sets real feature, customization, and automation limits, which directly affects what an analyst finds in an org.

questions.q: Which edition is described as the most common tier for mid-size and larger companies, with deep customization and API access?
options: Enterprise
Essentials
Professional
Unlimited only
questions.explain: Enterprise Edition is the most common tier for mid-size and larger companies, opening up deeper customization and API access than Essentials or Professional.

questions.q: If an analyst expects a field or automation to exist but it doesn't, what should they check first, per this lesson?
options: Whether the org's edition actually supports that feature, before assuming the data is broken
Whether the field was deleted by a hacker
Nothing — this situation is always a data quality bug
Whether Salesforce's servers are down
questions.explain: A missing feature may simply be a licensing/edition limitation, not a data quality problem.

questions.q: What is the AppExchange, per this lesson?
options: Salesforce's official marketplace for third-party apps that install directly into an org
A Salesforce edition tier above Unlimited
An internal Salesforce reporting tool
A synonym for Sales Cloud
questions.explain: The AppExchange is Salesforce's real app marketplace, similar in spirit to a mobile app store but for enterprise software.

questions.q: Why might an analyst find a field or object that isn't documented anywhere in standard Salesforce docs?
options: It may have been added by an installed AppExchange app as a custom object or custom field
Standard Salesforce documentation always covers every possible field in every org
Undocumented fields are always a sign of a corrupted org
Salesforce randomly generates unnamed fields for every org
questions.explain: AppExchange apps often bring their own custom objects and fields, which are org-specific and won't appear in generic Salesforce documentation.
